methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Tech researchers look to AI to ease difficult workplace conversations
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researchers developing proprietary AI coaching tools signals deep capability building, but concentration in academic institutions rather than distribution to workplaces across Southwest/Southside regions where such tools might have highest impact.

signals.title: RiverStreet Networks removed from multiple broadband deployment projects in rural Virginia after years of delays
signals.signal_reading: Broadband infrastructure failure affecting 30,000+ rural customers directly undermines the connectivity prerequisite for any AI adoption—shallow or deep—locking Southwest/Southside into capability isolation regardless of training initiatives elsewhere.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional commitment to building deep AI fluency for future leaders, potentially creating distributed expertise if graduates remain regionally rather than concentrating in NoVA/Richmond metros.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops explicitly targeting technology gap closure signals grassroots capability distribution, though sustainability and depth beyond introductory training will determine whether this becomes shallow platform adoption or genuine fluency building.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership combining university research capacity with community-focused education infrastructure creates potential for distributed deep learning beyond traditional tech corridors, though Richmond Metro benefits may not extend to Southside/Southwest without intentional reach.
